reason: The low tether should keep the first lift contained; it is the only offered action.
expectation: I expect the whale to be secured for a low test, though the other safety equipment may still need fitting.

effect: The whale is tethered; the landing cradle is the next available preparation.
reaction: A sensible safety step, though the result adds little detail.
reason: The cradle should cushion the low test landing, and it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the cradle to be positioned beneath the tethered whale for the test.

effect: The whale is now above the padded landing area, ready for further test preparations.
reaction: Another sensible but predictable safety step.
reason: The control lead is the only offered combination and should allow the lift to be operated from a distance.
expectation: I expect the lead to connect to the lift controls so the whale can be tested safely.

effect: The lift works, but the dragon end is too heavy, so the balance needs adjustment before further testing.
reaction: The uneven hover makes the balance problem concrete.
reason: The counterweight handle is the only offered combination and should help correct the nose-heavy tilt.
expectation: I expect to move the counterweight toward the rear, although a level may be needed to check the result.

effect: The counterweight adjustment produced a rebalanced whale; the level can check it.
reaction: The result is brief, so I’m curious how well the adjustment worked.
reason: The bubble level is the only offered combination and should verify the whale’s balance.
expectation: I expect to check whether the whale sits level, possibly revealing whether further adjustment is needed.

effect: The level confirms that the counterweight balanced the hovering whale; the emergency stop remains to be tested.
reaction: It is satisfying to see an ordinary balance adjustment solve the tilt.
reason: The stop cord is the only offered combination and should allow the emergency stop to be tested.
expectation: I expect the lever and cord to activate the stop button and bring the whale down onto its padded landing area.

effect: The stop cord successfully cut lift, and I learned that an emergency drop differs from a controlled landing.
reaction: The distinction between stopping immediately and landing gently made the test more meaningful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Checking the rebalanced hover was most worthwhile: the bubble level showed how an ordinary counterweight corrected the whale’s tilt.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the landing cradle was sensible but predictable, with little detail in the result.

surprise.text: The stop test made clear that cutting lift immediately drops the whale, rather than landing it gently.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though each step offered only one combination, leaving little room for a meaningful choice.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the fair flies beyond the low test, though I would hope for more choices along the way.
